text:
maria: heads up — deployed a 5% canary with header guard (X-Canary: canary) and seeing skew. a lot more traffic still routed to primary than expected.

maria: quick snapshot from logs: `routing_policy=header_then_sticky`, requests with header present are still being routed to v1 with `routing_decision=sticky` and cookie rw_sticky=abcd1234.

devon: can you paste the canary config from the console? maybe ordering got inverted when the rollout was created.

maria: console snippet: ```json
{
  "rollout": "service-foo",
  "strategy": "traffic_split",
  "guards": ["header:X-Canary"],
  "sticky": {"cookie": "rw_sticky", "by": "session_id"},
  "weights": {"primary": 95, "canary": 5}
}```

li: if guards are evaluated first, header should short-circuit sticky. but our runtime docs say sticky can override guards if cookie exists. that might be the root cause.

sam: saw similar before — sticky maps keep users pinned even when new guards are introduced. we added a migration to invalidate sticky keys on major rollout changes but i guess header-only canaries are considered non-major.

maria: reproduced locally with `curl -H 'X-Canary: canary' -b 'rw_sticky=abcd1234'`: still gets `x-runtime-version: v1`.

sam: minimal repro: ```bash
# should route to canary but returns v1
curl -i -H 'X-Canary: canary' -b 'rw_sticky=abcd1234' https://api.redwood.local/generate
```

devon: ok — two possible fixes: 1) change guard evaluation to run before sticky OR 2) when a guard condition is present on the request, ignore sticky for that request. option 2 is less risky.

li: UX ask: console should show which users are pinned (sticky map) and allow invalidation per rollout. that'll help ops avoid flaky canaries.

maria: agreed. for now we need a hotfix. sam — can you push a runtime patch to short-circuit sticky when header guard matched?

sam: i can patch and roll a canary today. implementation is one-line: if (guardMatched(request)) { bypassSticky(); } — but need tests.

devon: please add telemetry flag `sticky_bypass.reason=guard` so we can query logs and confirm behavior.

sam: will do. also adding a rolling invalidation endpoint: `POST /admin/rollouts/{id}/invalidate-sticky` to clear sticky keys for that rollout id.

maria: thanks. what's the plan for retroactive cleanup of already pinned sessions that should go to canary?

sam: invalidate endpoint will clear them. i'll run it for the service after the patch lands. schedule: patch -> canary -> roll -> invoke invalidate -> increase traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime/patch/sticky-guard-bypass -> canary (10% nodes).

maria: monitoring: please watch 200s, latency, and error budget plus `sticky_bypass.count`.

li: filed a console ticket to surface sticky maps and an action button: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-4521

devon: follow-up question: should we change default sticky key from `session_id` to `user_id`? session_id makes canaries useless for logged-out flows.

maria: that would be breaking for some customers; prefer opt-in. add as a roadmap item.

sam: patch is on canary, telemetry shows `sticky_bypass.reason=guard` for requests with X-Canary. early metrics: canary traffic matches header % now.

maria: great. i'm going to run `invalidate-sticky` for the last 48h active keys after the canary finishes. please coordinate before increasing to 50%.

deploy-bot: canary health OK -> promoted to 50% after 30m.

maria: closing this thread after rollout completes, and tracking console work on PLAT-4521. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
